_purpose: GAP-2026-08-15-PYQCOUNT-DRIVE-ACQUISITION, patch P7 — the class-level fix. A remediation that establishes a LAW must be applied to EVERY spec the law governs, and the completeness of that application must be MACHINE-CHECKABLE. GAP-2026-07-26-003 was remediated file-by-file from a changelog list; the PYQ counting path was not on that list; five days later a file split copied the unfixed text forward 'content byte-identical' into a file that never mentions the GAP id. A law enforced by a checklist is a law that will be re-broken by the next file split.
_enforced_by: audit_sync.py. This file is DATA, not documentation: audit_sync hard-fails if it is missing, malformed, or out of step with the corpus.
_derived_not_declared: The 'governs' list is CHECKED AGAINST THE CORPUS, never trusted. Any spec that performs a governed operation but is absent from 'governs' is a FAIL — that is the half a hand-maintained list can never provide, and it is the half that failed in July. Adding a spec to 'governs' does not exempt it from anything; it subscribes it to 'verified_by'.
_on_file_split: Any file split MUST re-run audit_sync against BOTH halves before the split is committed. The 2026-07-31 PYQAnalyse v2.29 -> PYQCount v1.0 split is precisely how this defect entered production.

EXECUTION-BOUNDARY-LAW.requires: A tool call cannot happen inside a running python process. Every spec performing a CLASS T operation must declare it as a tagged pass-bodied stub AND inject a RESOLVER over already-materialised results at every injection point. Never inject the CLASS T marker name itself, and never inject a name the spec does not bind.
EXECUTION-BOUNDARY-LAW.detect_note: A spec PERFORMS this operation when its text contains a live (non-comment) call to a documented injection point — audit_callgraph.INJECTION_POINTS. Commented-out historical examples do not count; a spec is expected to quote the defect it fixed.
